À 19 ans, Blaise Pascal commence une mac: At 19, Blaise Pascal starts an adding machine to help his father, in charge of taxes in Rouen. He presents it in 1645.
Le 1er février 1673, Leibniz montre à la: On February 1, 1673, Leibniz shows the Royal Society the wooden model of his machine. His stepped drum will be used right up to the calculators of the 1970s.
Le 23 décembre 1801, Jacquard brevète un: On December 23, 1801, Jacquard patents a mechanism that reads the pattern from punched cards. Changing the pattern means changing the cards.
Babbage décrit une machine avec un mouli: Babbage describes a machine with a mill that calculates, a store that remembers and cards that give orders. It will never be built.
Ada Lovelace publie ses notes sur la mac: Ada Lovelace publishes her notes on the Analytical Engine. Note G sets out the calculation of a Bernoulli number, operation by operation.
Au MIT, Claude Shannon montre que l'algè: At MIT, Claude Shannon shows that Boolean algebra describes relay circuits. Published in 1938, his thesis founds the design of digital circuits.
Le 21 juin 1948, la Baby de Manchester e: On June 21, 1948, the Manchester Baby runs, for the first time, a program stored in its electronic memory.
Grace Hopper termine le système A-0, l'u: Grace Hopper completes the A-0 system, one of the first compilers. "Nobody believed that," she would say.
